title: Can't build with `threads=no` on Linux following the introduction of SDL
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.5.stable
- Not reproducible in: 4.4.1.stable

### System information

Godot v4.6.dev (8d8041bd4) - Fedora Linux 42 (KDE Plasma Desktop Edition) on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (nvidia; 580.82.09) - AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D 16-Core Processor (32 threads) - 62.33 GiB memory

### Issue description

I can't build Godot with `threads=no` on Linux following the introduction of SDL.

For context, `threads=no` isn't exclusive to web platforms. It can also be used on desktop platforms, mainly for testing purposes and checking if race conditions are the source of a bug. This build option has been available on desktop platforms for a few months, but the introduction of SDL broke the build when using `threads=no`:

As a workaround, you can compile with `sdl=no` as well, but this will impact controller support.
